To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a regulated membrane recycling pathway is the principal means for the parietal cell to redistribute its apical H,K-ATPS-rich membranes; 2) a signal transduction pathway is required for the initiation of the membrane recycling process and involves the GTPase Rab11 and the protein kinase A; 3) the membrane recycling pathway requires the coordinated action of several membrane targeting proteins, including the small GTPase Rab4; 4) the membrane recycling process requires membrane docking

the H,K-ATPAse, the proton pump of parietal cells, is recycled between an endosomal compartment and the apical surface of these cells in a regulated fashion, and that the actin cyto-skeleton is essential for the recycling process.
the H,K-ATAse is a highly regulated transporter whose apical surface density is determined by the rate of its recycling from the tubulovesicular membrane compartment to the apical membrane.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the parietal cell is a highly regulated system for the rapid and massive redistribution of H,K pumps to the apical surface.
parietal cell membrane recycling involves the concerted action of several membrane trafficking pathways and the actin cytoplasmic network.
the parietal cell membrane recycling pathway is highly regulated, and the molecular mechanisms that underpin the pathway are complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the parietal cell membrane recycling pathway has been conserved through eukaryotic evolution and is a paradigm of membrane traffic in polarized epithelia.
membrane recycling is a general mechanism that is used by many cells to move membrane proteins to and from the cell surface.

membrane recycling, which is an essential component of many physiological membrane trafficking processes, is a highly regulated process that is controlled by a complex array of signaling pathways, cytoskeletal proteins, membrane targeting proteins, and membrane docking and fusion proteins, all working in concert to achieve the ultimate goal of moving a membrane transporter from one cellular compartment to another.
